name: repo-identity-guard
description: Lock a Git repository to an explicitly chosen Git/GitHub identity, and keep private notes per repository.

commands.title: Repo Identity Guard: Assign Identity to Current Repository
Repo Identity Guard: Change Assigned Identity
Repo Identity Guard: Unlock Current Repository
Repo Identity Guard: Repair Identity Lock
Repo Identity Guard: Check Identity Lock (verifies push account)
Repo Identity Guard: Use Assigned Identity in Git Config

repoIdentityGuard.identities.markdownDescription: Reusable identities (e.g. Work, Personal). An identity does nothing on its own: a repository is only locked when you explicitly assign an identity to it ("Repo Identity Guard: Assign Identity to Current Repository"). Repositories are never matched to identities automatically. User settings only — a workspace cannot define identities.

id.description: Stable unique id. Locks record it so later edits to this identity can be detected.

label.description: Short display label, e.g. Work or Personal.

gitName.description: Expected Git author/committer name. Omit to enforce only the email.

gitEmail.description: Expected Git author/committer email. Always enforced in locked repositories.

expectedGitHubLogin.description: The github.com username every push from a locked repository must authenticate as (what `ssh -T git@<alias>` reports). Not your email, not the repository owner. Required for a complete identity: while it is missing, commits are still locked but EVERY push from a repository locked to this identity is blocked. Also requires at least one trusted SSH host alias, otherwise every push is blocked.

trustedSshHostAliases.description: SSH host aliases (Host entries in ~/.ssh/config, e.g. github-work) that pushes for this identity must use. Each must resolve to github.com with IdentitiesOnly yes; the account is still verified live on every push.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Notes (add, edit, delete, search, copy, export, import) work in untrusted workspaces — they are local data that is never executed. Assigning, changing, repairing or unlocking an identity lock installs or removes Git hooks, and using the assigned identity in Git config writes repository Git config, so all of those actions require Workspace Trust; legacy Shield installations are also only migrated once the workspace is trusted.
